newsitem.title: USA: Senator-Sourdough project may need ANWR drilling.
newsitem.headline: Senator-Sourdough project may need ANWR drilling.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Frank Murkowski of Alaska said Monday the federal government might have to allow drilling in the Artic National Wildlife Refuge to see whether oil found near the refuge might also lie under ANWR.
British Petroleum and Chevron last week announced a new oil discovery called the Sourdough prospect in Alaska near the border of ANWR. The find is believed to be commercially viable.

Before the companies can start developing the find, which is on a state lease, they would have to determine whether oil that they pump up might also come from beneath the Arctic refuge, which is federal property.

"The structure potentially could go under ANWR," Murkowski said in a speech to the National Ocean Industries Association. Murkowski told reporters that it would be the Interior Department's responsibility to see if there was oil in ANWR, an area that the Clinton Administration has refused to open to drilling.
"Who does that oil belong to," Murkowski told reporters after his speech.
Murkowski said the only way to determine whether drilling on the state lease might suck oil from under ANWR might be to drill in the refuge.
"The only way to find out is to see if there's oil on the other side," he told reporters.
